h1: The 6 Best Gas Backpack Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Gas Backpack Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six gas backpack leaf blowers from Husqvarna, HASANEN, HTK, PROYAMA and Thalorus, with airflow figures and what each costs you.
summary: The Husqvarna 150BT is the best gas backpack blower for buyers who want a proven brand at a sensible price. The 570BTS is the premium step-up. HASANEN lists the highest airflow at 850 CFM for the least money, the HTK is a balanced mid-tier import, and the Thalorus favors wind speed. PROYAMA's big engine comes with few figures.
intro: Gas backpack blowers get judged on CFM, but airflow is only half the story. The odd pattern in this category is that the loudest spec claims come from little-known brands with thin documentation, while the proven names often publish almost no figures at all. Choosing by the biggest number alone can leave you with a machine nobody will service.

We reviewed six gas backpack blowers and ranked them on what the listings state: airflow, wind speed, engine size and price tier. Where a listing gives no number, we say so and weigh brand history instead. The result is a ranking that balances claimed output against support you can actually count on.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A backpack-format Husqvarna that balances proven name and price tier.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 150BT is a gas backpack blower from a long-established brand, in the $200 to $500 tier. The listing gives no CFM or MPH figure, so its case rests on format and name.

It ranks first because it pairs the backpack carry with the strongest support network in the group. The imports below promise bigger numbers for less money, yet a mower dealer can service a Husqvarna, and parts are easy to find. Against the 570BTS, it asks far less for what appears to be the same basic job.

Buy it if you want a reliable backpack blower and plan to keep it for years. The caveat is that you cannot compare it by airflow, because the listing omits the figures. Check the manufacturer's page for CFM and MPH before you order, and decide whether those numbers satisfy your yard.
products.idealFor: Buyers who value a proven brand.

products.name: Husqvarna 570BTS Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The step-up Husqvarna backpack, in the $500+ tier.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 570BTS is the step-up backpack blower from the same maker, listed in the $500+ tier. Like the 150BT, the listing offers very few figures.

Second place comes from an uneven value story. It costs far more than the 150BT, yet the page gives you no extra numbers that justify the jump. You are buying into a premium model by reputation, so it stays above the imports only because the brand is proven and the backpack design suits long jobs.

Buy it if you want the top Husqvarna and are willing to verify its specifications on the maker's site. Skip it if you want strong value, because the 150BT delivers the same format and name for much less. The most expensive blower here is not necessarily the best one for a typical yard.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the premium Husqvarna.

products.name: HASANEN Backpack Gas Powered Leaf Blower
products.description:
The HASANEN is a gas backpack blower listing 850 CFM, the highest airflow in the ranking, at the $50 to $100 tier, the lowest price here.

It sits third because the number is a manufacturer claim from a brand with little track record. On paper it beats every Husqvarna, and it costs a fraction of their price, which is a strong argument for budget buyers. But the listing gives no MPH figure, and support is uncertain if the engine or harness fails.

Buy it if you want maximum stated airflow on a tight budget and accept the risk. Skip it if brand support matters to you. If you would rather give up some airflow for a clearer spec sheet, the HTK below lists both CFM and MPH.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want maximum airflow.

products.name: HTK Backpack Blower
products.verdict: 665 CFM and 205 MPH in the middle price tier.
products.description:
The HTK backpack blower lists 665 CFM and 205 MPH, in the $100 to $200 tier. It is the one import here that publishes both airflow and wind speed alongside a mid-range price.

It ranks fourth because it gives up 185 CFM to the HASANEN while costing more, so the cheaper blower wins on airflow per dollar. What the HTK offers in return is a fuller spec sheet, which makes it easier to judge than the PROYAMA below. Its wind speed is also higher than the Husqvarna listings can show.

Buy it if you have a mid-size yard and want to see real figures before you pay. Skip it if you want the most airflow, or the comfort of a well-known service network. It is a balanced blower, not a standout in any single area.

products.name: Thalorus 52cc Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 52cc engine with 550 CFM and 230 MPH.
products.description:
The Thalorus uses a 52cc gas engine and lists 550 CFM and 230 MPH, in the $100 to $200 tier. The 230 MPH wind speed is the highest in the ranking.

It lands fifth because its airflow is the lowest among the blowers that list one, trailing the HTK by 115 CFM. Speed helps lift wet and matted leaves, which is a real advantage on an autumn lawn, but a pile that is large and dry needs volume more than velocity.

Buy it if your main problem is stuck, damp debris and you value fast air. Skip it if you clear big dry piles, where the HASANEN or HTK would do the job quicker. As with other imports here, confirm the warranty terms and replacement parts before buying.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer high wind speed.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 72cc engine with few other figures listed.
products.description:
The PROYAMA lists a 72cc gas engine in a backpack format, in the $100 to $200 tier. It carries the largest engine in the group, but the listing offers no airflow or wind speed.

It ranks last because there is no way to compare it on paper. Engine displacement alone does not prove a blower is strong, since fan design and nozzle shape matter too. Against the HTK and Thalorus, which publish both CFM and MPH, it asks you to trust the cc number and nothing else.

Buy it if you specifically want a big engine and you can confirm the performance figures elsewhere. Skip it if you decide by CFM, because the page gives you none. Ask the seller for the airflow and speed ratings before you place an order.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a big engine.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air a blower pushes out each minute, which sets how quickly you clear a pile. Look for the number in the title or specs, not a vague power claim. The HASANEN lists 850 CFM, while the Husqvarna pages list none.

MPH is the speed of the air leaving the nozzle. It lifts wet, stuck leaves that volume alone leaves behind. The Thalorus lists 230 MPH and the HTK 205 MPH. Together with CFM, it describes real clearing ability, so check that both figures appear.

Engine size in cc is the displacement of the two-stroke engine. A bigger engine can mean more power, but fan and nozzle design change the result. The PROYAMA lists 72cc and the Thalorus 52cc. Treat cc as one clue, and confirm CFM and MPH before drawing conclusions.

Brand support is what happens after the sale: parts, repairs and warranty claims. Established makers such as Husqvarna have dealers who can service the machine, while imports may not. Check the brand, the warranty on the listing and whether replacement parts are sold separately.

A backpack format moves the weight onto your shoulders and hips, which matters on large yards and long sessions. All six picks here are backpacks. Confirm the word backpack in the title, and check that the harness is padded and adjustable, since comfort affects how long you can work.

faq.a: It is a blower worn on your back with the engine behind you, so the weight sits on your shoulders instead of one arm. That makes the Husqvarna 150BT and the other picks comfortable for long jobs.
Comparing only CFM. The HASANEN lists 850 CFM, but brand support and MPH matter too. A Husqvarna 150BT may list less, yet it comes with dealer servicing that cheaper imports often lack.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna worth it over the HASANEN?
faq.a: If you want brand support, yes. The 150BT is a proven name with a dealer network. If airflow per dollar is the priority, the HASANEN lists far more CFM for a much lower price.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Follow the maker's fuel mix guidance in the manual, adjust the harness straps so the weight sits on your hips, and prime the engine before pulling the cord. Check the mix ratio for the HTK or Thalorus.
Use fresh fuel mixed at the correct ratio, keep the air filter clean and wipe debris off the cooling fins after use. Run the tank dry before storing a blower like the Husqvarna 150BT for winter.
The PROYAMA lists the largest engine at 72cc. The Thalorus follows at 52cc. The other four listings do not state engine size, so compare them by their airflow and wind speed instead.

finalTake: The Husqvarna 150BT is the best gas backpack blower for buyers who value a proven brand and straightforward servicing. The 570BTS is a premium step up, and the HASANEN is the budget gamble for maximum claimed airflow. Choose the HTK for a fuller spec sheet and the Thalorus when wind speed matters most.
